correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly defines uniform crossing-pair multiplicities and handles all \(n\ge4\) including the even midpoint. Exact four-gap composition gives the finite probability formula. Riemann summation gives the limiting density; the \(0\le q<2\) uniform integrability bound, critical harmonic-sum comparison and supercritical dominated-convergence bound \(C_q k^{1-q}\) establish every fixed \(q\ge0\). An independent Euclidean coordinate implementation enumerated ALL four-subsets for n=4..24 and exactly recovered integer frequencies; independent integration and large-size moment computations corroborated the constants. The computational checks are not used in lieu of analytic limiting arguments.

originality.rationale: The angular SUPPORT was already described by Arikushi–Tóth, and the spatial intersection count by Poonen–Rubinstein. The present claim is the exact pair-multiplicity-weighted angular mass function, its continuous density and the three inverse-sine moment asymptotic regimes including the logarithmic threshold and convergent zeta-series constants; none was supplied or implied by the inspected nearest source statements. The source comparisons and relevant published mathematical records support provisional originality only, not absolute priority.

value.rationale: Reciprocal sine is an intrinsic transversality determinant for two crossing lines. Conditioning by this determinant is naturally important for robustness and geometric intersection computations. Its finite-n distribution with a sharp cutoff and limiting \(z^{-2}\) tail yield a meaningful critical order \(\(q=2\)\), a nontrivial logarithmic coefficient and higher-order zeta constants. The result completes the exact law on a canonical model rather than arbitrarily selecting a small numerical subproblem.
